title: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC

claims.text: Davis and Goadrich showed a deep connection between the two curve spaces at the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning in 2006, pages 233 to 240: a curve dominates in one space if and only if it dominates in the other. They also establish practical consequences — that linear interpolation between points is incorrect in the precision-recall space, and that algorithms optimising the area under one curve are not guaranteed to optimise the area under the other.

source.title: Jesse Davis and Mark Goadrich, The relationship between Precision-Recall and ROC curves, Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning, pages 233-240, 2006, doi 10.1145/1143844.1143874

claims.text: Their summary of when each applies: when the class distribution is close to uniform the first kind of curve has many desirable properties, but with a highly skewed dataset the second gives a more accurate picture of an algorithm's performance.

source.title: Jesse Davis and Mark Goadrich, The relationship between Precision-Recall and ROC curves, Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning, pages 233-240, 2006, doi 10.1145/1143844.1143874

beats.broke: a classifier makes two kinds of mistake, they have different consequences, and a single proportion of correct answers adds them together and reports the sum
beats.fix: count the four cells of the confusion matrix separately and build the measures that answer specific questions — how many flagged items were right, how many real cases were caught — then choose by which error is costly
beats.cost: each measure answers one question and ignores the others, the threshold-free summaries hide the threshold you will actually have to pick, and improving the area under one curve does not guarantee improving the area under another
beats.interview: which measure to report, and what fixes the answer
